title: Hysteresis Demonstrator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Hysteresis
Thresholds
Sensor Noise
Auto Brightness
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim comparing a single threshold with hysteresis on a noisy light-sensor reading. Sliders set the noise and the upper and lower thresholds, and counters show how many times each output switches.

educational.topic: Hysteresis and dead zones for noisy sensors
learningObjectives: Analyze why a single threshold chatters when a noisy signal hovers near it
Explain how a dead zone between two thresholds removes chatter
Choose a gap that is wide enough for the noise but still responds to real changes
prerequisites: Reading a light sensor with the ADC

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Comparison of two strategies on the same data
keyQuestions: Why does the single-threshold output switch many times in a row?
How wide must the dead zone be for a given amount of noise?
What is the cost of a very wide dead zone?
commonMisconceptions: Averaging alone always removes flicker (it reduces noise but a slow signal can still hover at the line)
A wider gap is always better (it makes the display slow to respond to real changes)
assessmentOpportunities: Record switch counts for several gaps and noise levels
Explain the trade-off of a very wide gap

controls.label: Start / Pause
controls.description: Scrolls new readings in. Opens paused with a full window of readings.
